arguments.conclusion: Money printing that is not evenly distributed transfers real wealth from those who receive the new money last to those who receive it first.

arguments.premise_synthesis: Money is loaned into existence, so each dollar adds future demand. First recipients spend at prices that have not yet changed, gaining real purchasing power. Later recipients face higher prices from the cumulative demand, eroding their purchasing power.
arguments.conclusion_supported: The claim that unevenly distributed money printing in a fiat system causes a transfer of real purchasing power from later recipients to earlier recipients, illustrating a structural critique of the monetary system.
